cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Income – money received, especially on a regular basis, for work or through investments.

p.em: Example: Getting a secondary source of income dramatically reduced her monthly stress.

cosy-blockquote.p: Leisure time ≠ working hours – time free from work or duties ≠ time spent performing professional obligations.

p.em: Example: He spent his leisure time playing acoustic guitar, far away from his grueling working hours.

cosy-blockquote.p: To accumulate – to gather or acquire an increasing number or quantity of something over time.

p.em: Example: He worked eighty hours a week simply to accumulate wealth he had no time to enjoy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Financial security – the peace of mind you feel when you have enough money to cover your expenses and emergencies.

p.em: Example: For many young adults, financial security is far more important than buying luxury brands.

cosy-blockquote.p: Affluence ≠ poverty – the state of having a great deal of money or wealth ≠ the state of being extremely poor.

p.em: Example: Living in extreme affluence can occasionally blind people to the painful realities of modern poverty.

cosy-blockquote.p: Burnout – physical or mental collapse caused by overwork or stress.

p.em: Example: She had to take a two-month leave of absence to recover from severe professional burnout.

cosy-blockquote.p: Fulfillment – the feeling of absolute satisfaction and happiness with your life achievements and goals.

p.em: Example: He found genuine artistic fulfillment in writing short stories rather than chasing corporate bonuses.

cosy-blockquote.p: To prioritize – to treat a specific goal or duty as being more important than other things.

p.em: Example: To save his mental health, he decided to prioritize slow leisure time over career advancement.

cosy-blockquote.p: Workaholism – an obsessive or compulsive need to work, often damaging one's personal life.

p.em: Example: In many competitive corporate cultures, workaholism is praised as a positive trait.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gratification – pleasure, especially when gained from the satisfaction of a desire.

p.em: Example: Shopping online offers instant gratification, but the happiness is extremely short-lived.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
A: A high income allows you to travel in absolute luxury and buy comfort. B: Having abundant leisure hours keeps you physically fit and calm.
★ Do you think a higher monthly income would solve most of your daily worries?

A: Spending your leisure time with loved ones builds deep, beautiful memories. B: Dedicating long hours to your career builds a powerful, respected network.
★ How do you protect your precious leisure time from office emails?

A: Working hard to accumulate savings prepares you for early retirement. B: Taking regular breaks during the year allows you to enjoy youth.
★ Are you actively trying to accumulate assets, or do you prefer spending?

A: Absolute financial security frees you from survival anxiety and fear. B: Living with minimal expenses teaches you true resourcefulness.
★ At what age do you hope to achieve complete financial security?

A: Living in affluence allows you to support charities and help family. B: Living simply prevents the stress of maintaining expensive possessions.
★ Does living in a highly wealthy neighborhood make people happier or more competitive?

A: Prioritizing mental health keeps your body completely free from burnout. B: Pushing your limits at work occasionally leads to extraordinary promotions.
★ Have you ever experienced professional burnout? How did you recover?

A: Finding deep fulfillment in creative hobbies is extremely satisfying. B: Reaching a high sales target at work brings great pride and energy.
★ Where do you find more genuine fulfillment: in your career or hobbies?

A: Deciding to prioritize family shows a healthy, balanced character. B: Prioritizing your company builds long-term wealth and power.
★ How do you prioritize your tasks when everything seems urgent?

A: Conquering workaholism allows you to rediscover slow, beautiful pleasures. B: An intense dedication to work keeps you focused and away from lazy habits.
★ Do you consider yourself a victim of mild workaholism?

A: Delaying gratification helps you build massive long-term wealth. B: Enjoying instant gratification keeps your daily morale high and joyful.
★ Are you good at delaying gratification for long-term goals?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
A: A low monthly income makes it impossible to afford high-quality education. B: High earnings often require sacrificing your physical and mental health.
★ Have you ever turned down a high-paying job because of the long hours?

A: Endless leisure time can lead to deep boredom and lack of purpose. B: Infinite working hours completely destroy your social life and marriage.
★ Do you find long vacations relaxing, or do you start to feel unproductive?

A: Refusing to accumulate savings leaves you vulnerable to sudden crises. B: Obsessing over accumulation turns you into a cold, greedy individual.
★ What is the absolute most useless thing you have accumulated?

A: Chasing financial security can trap you in a boring, uninspiring career. B: Having zero security makes every daily expense highly stressful.
★ Have you ever stayed in a boring job solely for the steady paycheck?

A: Living in extreme affluence alienates you from simple, real-world friends. B: Living in poverty stops you from pursuing creative artistic dreams.
★ Do you think wealth makes it harder to find authentic, loyal friends?

A: Pushing yourself to burnout can permanently damage your nervous system. B: Avoiding all pressure makes you lazy and unprepared for life's challenges.
★ What are the early warning signs of burnout in your body?

A: Seeking fulfillment solely in hobbies can delay your career success. B: Seeking fulfillment solely in your corporate title is highly dangerous.
★ Has your concept of personal fulfillment changed since you left school?

A: If you fail to prioritize your health, no amount of wealth can save you. B: Failing to prioritize your duties can lead to sudden professional failure.
★ What is the hardest thing you had to deprioritize this year?

A: Chronic workaholism is a socially accepted addiction that ruins children. B: Having no professional ambition makes you look lazy in modern dating.
★ Do you think modern society rewards workaholism too much?

A: Pursuing instant gratification ruins your long-term focus and discipline. B: Delaying all gratification makes you a dry, unhappy person.
★ What is your favorite form of instant gratification after a hard day?

ul.li: Incorrect: We discussed about our working hours → Correct: We discussed our working hours (('Discuss' is transitive and does not take the preposition 'about'))
Incorrect: I prefer leisure time than working hours → Correct: I prefer leisure time to working hours ((Use 'prefer A to B', not 'than'))
Incorrect: The burnout made me to leave my job → Correct: The burnout made me leave my job ((The causative verb 'make' is followed by a bare infinitive without 'to'))
